;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**At least 43 Afghan soldiers are killed in a [[Taliban]] attack on an army base in [[Kandahar Province]]. Around 10 Taliban fighters also died in the attack. [http://www.businessinsider.com/ap-taliban-attack-army-camp-in-southern-afghanistan-killing-43-2017-10 (''Business Insider'')]
*[[2017 Tongo Tongo ambush]]
**The [[United States Africa Command]] sends a team to [[Niger]] to investigate an October 4 ambush which killed four U.S. soldiers. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/africa/pentagon-sends-team-niger-find-out-what-went-wrong-n812121 (NBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in Florida]]
**Two people are arrested and five people suffer minor injuries at the [[University of Florida]] during protests of [[Richard B. Spencer]]'s speech at an event there. [http://abcnews.go.com/US/security-ramped-white-nationalist-richard-spencers-florida-event/story?id=50585570 (ABC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish Prime Minister]] [[Mariano Rajoy]] warns [[President of Catalonia|Catalonian President]] [[Carles Puigdemont]] that the region's [[Autonomous communities of Spain|autonomy]] will be suspended if he fails to drop the [[Executive Council of Catalonia|Catalonian government]]'s bid for [[Catalan independence referendum, 2017|secession]] by 10:00 a.m. [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] (08:00 a.m. [[Greenwich Mean Time|GMT]]). [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-41675105 (BBC)]
**Rajoy announces that he will begin the process of stripping Catalonia of its autonomy starting on October 21. This follows a letter Puigdemont wrote before the deadline again asking for dialogue, and blaming Rajoy for escalating the crisis. Rajoy had wanted dialogue after reassurances that the independence bid was dropped. [https://www.vox.com/world/2017/10/19/16502872/spain-catalonia-conflict (Vox)]
*Aftermath of the [[2017 New Zealand general election]]
**[[New Zealand First]] leader [[Winston Peters]] chooses to create a minority [[coalition government|coalition]] with the [[Labour Party (New Zealand)|Labour Party]] and form the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|sixth Labour government]]. [http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11933639 (''NZ Herald'')]
**[[Jacinda Ardern]], the leader of the Labour Party, will be the next [[Prime Minister of New Zealand|prime minister]]. [http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/election/2017/10/nz-s-new-government-nz-first-chooses-labour.html (Newshub)]

;Science and technology
*Scientists studying flying insects in [[nature reserves]] and [[protected areas]] of [[western Germany]] report a decline of more than 75% of the population in about three decades. [https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2017/10/oh-no/543390/ (The Atlantic)] [http://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0185809 (PLOS One)]

;Sports
* [[2017 Major League Baseball postseason]]
** The [[2017 Los Angeles Dodgers season|Los Angeles Dodgers]] defeat the [[2016 Chicago Cubs season|defending]] [[World Series]] champion [[2017 Chicago Cubs season|Chicago Cubs]] 11–1 in Game 5 of the [[National League (baseball)|National League]] [[2017 National League Championship Series|Championship Series]], winning the series 4–1. This will be the [[Los Angeles Dodgers|Dodgers]]' first World Series appearance since [[1988 World Series|1988]]. [http://www.espn.com/mlb/recap?gameId=371019116 (AP via ESPN)]
